title: Compliance webhook gateway for configurable residency and retention proofs
creator: Ayesha Kumar
description:
Goal: Build a gateway service that receives, normalizes, and routes compliance-related events (audit, residency assertions, retention actions, evidence bundles) to downstream archival, notification, and verification systems. The gateway must support: 1) per-customer residency hints and immutable retention TTLs; 2) signed evidence bundling with KMS-backed keys; 3) idempotent delivery to external webhooks with at-least-once semantics and deduplication; 4) region-aware routing and proof-of-storage attachments for regulatory audits. The gateway will expose a compact REST contract for event ingestion and an asynchronous delivery queue for downstream consumers. Non-goals: not replacing the full event-store or long-term archive; archival responsibility remains with the archival service.

Design constraints: minimal latency for ack to callers (<200ms typical), configurable fanout limits per customer, backpressure propagation to avoid infinite retries, support for both synchronous and asynchronous evidence requests. Must be observable (per-event tracing, delivery metrics, SLA dashboards) and include a replay mechanism for reprocessing evidence bundles.

Contract (ingest POST /v1/compliance/events): payload: {"event_id":"uuid","customer_id":"cid-...","type":"audit|residency|retention","timestamp":"iso8601","region_hint":"eu-west-1","payload":{...},"retention_policy":{"ttl_days":90,"immutable":true},"evidence_refs":["s3://..."],"signature":{"key_id":"kms-key-1","sig":"base64"}}. The gateway verifies signature if present, enriches with ledger_id and store_location, and responds 202 with delivery_id. For synchronous evidence requests callers may request a signed receipt via ?receipt=true.

Security: signatures validated against customer KMS keys (customer-managed or Redwood-managed), payloads scanned for PII leakage before forwarding, audit logs written to WORM storage. Keys must rotate without breaking historical verification.

Delivery guarantees and retries: at-least-once to webhooks with exponential backoff, deduplication using event_id and content-hash for 30 days, delivery TTL configurable per customer (default 7 days). Failed deliveries generate evidence-alert events for on-call and customer webhooks if configured.

Observability & testability: unit + integration tests for signature validation, dedupe, and regional routing. Load test target: 5k events/s across clusters with median ack latency <200ms. Compliance test harness will replay sample events and validate proof bundles.
acceptance_criteria: API contract implemented and documented in Confluence with examples
Gateway accepts events and returns 202 with delivery_id in breadth tests at 5k events/s
Signed evidence bundles verifiable using stored keys (tests for key rotation)
Delivery deduplication prevents duplicate downstream side-effects within 30 days
Region hints respected: eu data stays in eu-backed archival endpoints per config
Metrics and traces for per-event delivery latency, success rate, and retries published to Console
implementation_notes: Create new service 'compliance-evidence-gateway' in runtime cluster with autoscaling group
Use existing KMS integration (ENG-75210) for signature validation and key lookup
Leverage event-queue (Kafka/topic compliance.events.{region}) and retention-enabled Kafka mirror for replay
Implement local LRU+persistent dedupe cache using Redis cluster with 30-day TTL and checkpointing
Add webhook delivery worker with concurrency limit per-customer and per-region circuit breakers
Provide admin endpoints for manual replay and per-customer configuration (fanout, delivery_ttl, sew)
Add e2e tests in github.com/redwood-inference/compliance-evidence-gateway with a PR template and CI matrix
